title: Current weekly teaching content
text:
This summary reflects the material currently in weekN/slides.qmd, including worked examples and solutions. It describes the slide decks themselves; the revised schedule labels are maintained separately in course_info.R.



Week
Topics covered in the current slides




Week 1
Descriptive statistics; data types and variables; an Excel primer on cell references, formulas, copying formulas and summary functions; populations and samples; measures of centre and spread, including variance, standard deviation and coefficient of variation; distribution shape; histograms and box plots; Excel Analysis ToolPak and visualisation exercises using real estate data.


Week 2
Probability rules, unions, conditional probability, mutually exclusive and independent events; frequency and relative-frequency tables; joint probabilities and PivotTables; applied categorical-data examples; probability as area under a density; normal and standard normal distributions, including Excel calculations.


Week 3
Sampling distributions and the Central Limit Theorem; sampling variability and standard errors; normal-distribution applications; confidence-interval estimation for means and proportions, including z and t intervals; applied retail, graduate-income, account-balance and survey examples.


Week 4
Sample proportions, their sampling distributions and standard errors, confidence intervals for proportions and an applied prevalence example; evidence-based hypothesis tests for population means and proportions; null and alternative hypotheses; test statistics and p-values; significance levels and decisions; marketing, transaction-success and business-process examples; Type I and Type II errors and test power.


Week 5
Chi-square test of independence for categorical variables, including expected counts and worked examples; scatterplots, covariance and correlation for numerical variables, with Excel formulas and cautions about nonlinear patterns and causation; simple linear regression in Excel, coefficient interpretation, prediction, slope confidence intervals, R^2 and slope tests using real-estate and marketing examples.


Week 6
Multiple regression and model evaluation using the ETF1100 Week 9 seminar and tutorial solutions: conditional slope interpretation, coefficient tests and model reduction, R^2 and residual diagnostics, dummy variables for categorical predictors, the overall F-test, and an Excel travel-time regression exercise with worked answers. The real-estate and travel-time source workbooks are linked from the Week 6 page.


Week 7
Introduction to time series; line charts of observed and deseasonalised values; time indexing and linear trend forecasts with Excel INTERCEPT and SLOPE; supplied seasonal indices and multiplicative forecasts; fitting on earlier training data, comparing forecasts with observed values in a later historical test period, then evaluating absolute errors with Excel ABS and mean absolute deviation (MAD). Worked examples use chocolate-bar and retail-sales data.


Week 8
Revision and examination practice; exam format and authorised materials; worked questions and solutions covering the unit’s statistical topics; closing reminders and source-page SETU material.

Select one:

for a large n, it says the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal, regardless of the shape of the population distribution.

for any population, it says the sampling distribution of the sample mean is approximately normal, regardless of the sample size.

for a large n, it says the population distribution is approximately normal, regardless of the shape of the sampling distribution.

Q3: Which of the following about the normal distribution is NOT true?
Select one:

Theoretically, the mean and median are the same.

Describe the sampling distribution of the mean waiting time between when the airplane taxis away from the terminal until the flight takes off for these 100 flights.
Select one:

H0: 𝛃1 = 0
H1: 𝛃1 > 0
Alpha: 0.05
p-value: 4.10E-02/2 = 2.05E-02
Decision: Reject H0 since p-value = 2.05E-02 < alpha = 0.05, at 5% significance level.
